name: Shackleton
features: Directly astride the rotational South Pole. Rim peaks receive up to ~86% annual sunlight; interior is permanently shadowed cold trap (< 90K) candidate for ice volatiles.

name: Faustini
features: Deep floor in perpetual shadow. Artemis candidate rim regions provide strategic communication line-of-sight to Earth.

name: Shoemaker
features: Target of Lunar Prospector impact (1999). Extremely cold floor with verified hydrogen signatures.

name: Haworth
features: Located near 0° longitude meridian. Deeply shadowed crater containing high priority volatile deposit indicators.

name: de Gerlache
features: Elevated ridge crests on the western rim connect toward Shackleton forming the famous 'Connecting Ridge'.

name: Malapert
features: Southwestern rim culminates in Malapert Mountain (Massif), rising ~5,000m above local datum with high direct-to-Earth visibility.

name: Amundsen
features: Large terraced crater with prominent central peak and stepped rim slopes. Northern and eastern rims receive favorable solar access.

name: Nobile
features: Selected exploration zone for robotic rover traverses due to diverse micro-PSR cold traps and traversable ridgelines.

name: Cabeus
features: Site of the NASA LCROSS impact (2009) which confirmed hydroxyl (OH) and water ice (5.5 wt%) in ejecta plume.

name: Sverdrup
features: Heavily shadowed polar floor between Shackleton and Amundsen.
